source.variation: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes H in three strokes: the left stem down, the crossbar from left to right, then the right stem down. (Its left-hand variant draws both stems first.) UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of H, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 62 of the 120 are three strokes (31 are one stroke, 27 two); in 55 of those 62 the first stroke is the left stem, drawn down, and the crossbar comes second in 37 and third in 25, so the adult writers split on its place; 60 draw it from left to right. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the H of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
